Jordan —

Quick take after skimming the draft: primary metric set I recommend we track in the platform dashboard during the run (real-time and 24h aggregated):
- Topline quality: Percentage of responses failing the promptset acceptance tests (we need a clear failure definition per prompt).
- Hallucination proxy: factuality-check failures on the curated subset (n=200).
- Safety signals: flagged content rate (from policy model) and manual review false-positive rate.
- Latency P95 / P99 for token generation across the sample workload.
- End-to-end cost delta (tokens * cost model) between A and B.

Sample sizes: for hallucination proxy and safety I suggest 200 labeled samples per variant to get ~5% margin; for acceptance tests we can use the full promptset (1,200 prompts) but sample review at n=300 per variant.

One more callout: we should instrument a "regression score" that weights severity (safety > hallucination > utility) so we can surface an aggregate. I'll attach a short spreadsheet with the scoring rubric in a follow-up.

Jonas

Subject: Re: Coordination: orchestration playbook + acceptance criteria for PromptSet A/B run

Thanks Jordan / Jonas —

Based on Jonas's metrics, here's a suggested acceptance checklist (concise):
1) Safety: no more than 0.3% increase in policy-flagged rate (manual review cap at 0.1% false positives).
2) Hallucination (factuality proxy): no increase > 2.0 percentage points on the n=200 sample.
3) Utility (QA): average user-satisfaction from blind eval (Likert 1-5) must not drop > 0.2 points.
4) Latency: P95 must not increase more than 30ms at target throughput.
5) Cost: per-response token spend delta must be within +/- 12% or show commensurate quality improvement.

Decision rule: if any safety threshold is violated -> immediate rollback and incident review. If hallucination or utility thresholds are violated -> hold rollout and convene triage (2-hour SLA for triage). If only cost exceeds the bar but quality improves, then product and sales (Jordan + Acme) decide.

For canary: run 5% traffic for 24 hours, then 25% for next 24h before full rollout if gates pass. For emergency fallback we should have a compatible smaller quantized model as a fast fallback — Dev, can you confirm latency and load for that fallback?

Marissa
Product QA Lead — Redwood Inference

All —

I validated infra windows for next week: we have an 18h low-traffic window on Wed 05/05 23:00 - Thu 05/06 17:00 PST where we can run the canary with minimal customer impact. I can reserve a dedicated pool (2x T4 equivalent) for the first 12 hours to tighten latency variance for the P95 measurement.

Fallback model: yes — we have a quantized variant (q6) already warmed in the us-west cluster; warm switch + routing change should take ~30s. We will instrument a soft-fallback route policy (traffic split 95/5 -> if regression score crosses threshold, flip to fallback route). However, flipping to fallback does not remove the new variant from rotation until we confirm fixes; it only preserves customer experience.

Data retention / logs: we can capture anonymized prompt-response pairs for the n=300 review, but Acme needs to confirm consent for storing snippets. Also, note that sampling and redaction will add ~10% overhead to storage pipeline.

Dev

Thanks for the plan. Quick leadership guidance: I want objective, measurable rollback gates. Marissa's thresholds look good. For the leadership decision bar, propose:
- Automatic fallback for safety violations only (as Marissa said) — immediate.
- For other regressions (hallucination/utility), if the regression score exceeds 0.6 (on Jonas's weighted rubric) we move to manual hold and a 4-hour incident review.
- Authorization to approve full rollout after canary should be by product + ops (Marissa + Dev) with Jordan notified; I will only intervene if the incident review recommends rollback or if the deal economics require escalation.

Also: Jordan, flag procurement (DataTrust) early if Acme confirms sample retention; legal will want a short addendum around PII redaction.

Laura
